questions.question: How many copies of a static variable exist when 50 objects of its class are created?
questions.explanation: A static variable belongs to the class, so there is exactly one copy no matter how many objects exist.

questions.question: class Gate { static int n = 0; Gate() { n++; } } ... new Gate(); new Gate(); new Gate(); System.out.println(Gate.n); What prints?
questions.explanation: All three constructors increase the same shared counter, so it ends at 3.

questions.question: class Bus { int seats = 40; static void show() { System.out.println(seats); } } Why does this fail to compile?
options: A static method cannot read an instance field directly
questions.explanation: A static method has no object, so there is no seats value to read without a reference.

questions.question: When does a static block run?
options: Every time an object is created
Every time a static method is called
Once, when the class is initialised
questions.explanation: The JVM runs static blocks once, on the first active use of the class.

questions.question: public class Hall { static { System.out.print("S"); } public static void main(String[] a) { System.out.print("M"); } } What prints?
questions.explanation: The class that holds main is initialised before main runs, so its static block prints first.

questions.question: Why is the main method declared static?
options: So the JVM can call it without creating an object
So it runs faster than other methods
So it can access instance fields
questions.explanation: No object exists when the program starts, so the JVM calls main on the class itself.

questions.question: class Pump { static void start() { this.log(); } void log() { } } What is wrong?
options: this cannot be used in a static method
questions.explanation: this means the current object, and a static method runs without any current object.

questions.question: What can you create without an instance of the outer class?
options: A local variable of the outer class
questions.explanation: A static nested class has no link to an outer object, so new Outer.Nested() works on its own.

questions.question: class Lamp { static String color = "red"; } ... Lamp a = new Lamp(); Lamp b = new Lamp(); a.color = "blue"; System.out.println(b.color); What prints?
questions.explanation: color is static, so a.color and b.color are the same shared variable.

questions.question: A child class declares a static method with the same signature as a static method in its parent. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Static methods are not overridden. The child method hides the parent one, and the reference type picks which runs.
